lines:
Responsibilities: Owns command handling and legal transitions for the one-Chat/one-Run/session lifecycle, coordinates first-input freezing, ordered later input, attempts, waits, approvals, pause/cancel, checkpoint, retry, fork, continue, and terminal inspection.
Owned state: ChatAggregateV1 rebuilt from canonical events: draft/version, phase, locked snapshotId, ordered input queue, active operation/attempt, wait or approval reference, worker generation/checkpoint cursor, lineage, and terminal reason. It owns no side-effect result outside committed evidence.
Public commands/events and ports: CreateDraft, StartChat, EnqueueInput, PauseRun, CancelRun, RetryCurrentOperation, ForkFromCheckpoint, ContinueInNewChat, RecordWorkerProposal, CheckpointRun, and ApplyCapabilityOutcome; emits typed ChatLifecycleEventV1 batches and WorkerControlEnvelopeV1.
Invariants: ChatId, RunId, and sessionId identify one object; only first input freezes a workflow. Busy ordinary input queues FIFO unless the frozen adapter explicitly supports steering. Terminal Chats reject ordinary input. Retry creates an attempt in the same Chat; editing/retrying older history and continue/fork create a new Chat with explicit lineage. Cancellation never implies undo of workspace effects.
Transactional and failure behavior: commands serialize per Chat using expected aggregate version and commandId. A transition becomes visible or is sent to a worker only after its event batch, snapshot/checkpoint reference, and required outbox effect commit atomically. Worker start/crash produces an inspectable degraded state and recoverable outbox; stale/duplicate proposals are rejected by generation, sequence, and attempt identity.
NFRs: deterministic reducers, concurrent progress across Chats, bounded queues/budgets, cancellation deadlines, trace correlation, and no UI blockage from worker failure.
Non-responsibilities: no graph scheduling, capability execution, direct storage writes, authority expansion, secret access, or side-effect replay.

Concurrent desktop Chats (2026-09-15): Selection is navigation only. Each admitted command owns an immutable ChatId/RunId, Chat-bound history and semantic committer, and a worker outside the desktop coordinator mutex. A per-Chat reservation serializes mutations while different Chats execute independently. Stop uses Chat-keyed tokens including the pre-registration window. Workers capture current configuration and credential metadata, sharing the existing host and ledger facilities. Provider-health and remembered-default feedback returns to the coordinator for application against current Settings. Short shared locks protect history-index and frozen-session writes and are never held during model/tool work. Active reservations distinguish live pending effects from crash recovery. Recovery, approvals, context editing, deletion and fork guards apply only to the target Chat. Preserve frozen authority, idempotency and canonical evidence.

User Stop and steering (2026-09-18): Stopping an unfinished built-in workflow response preserves a durable continuation of that pass: current node, completed node outputs and selected branches. The next accepted ordinary user message in that Chat steers the interrupted model/Agent node and then continues downstream; it must not rerun earlier planning or completed effects. Restore committed per-node model context and settled tool evidence, append the new user message once, and use fresh invocation identities. Stop cancels in-flight calls; cancelled or uncertain tools are not automatically replayed.
A workflow, Settings, or capability edit made before continuing is adopted for the remaining work: the resumed pass keeps its position, completed node outputs and selected branches, and resolves the current documents - tools newly enabled, changed node definitions, changed provider or budget settings - from that point on. Nothing already completed is re-run, and an edit never retro-fits a pass that already ran. A continuation must therefore remain usable in the same Chat where the user changed configuration in response to what the model reported as missing.
Persist and validate continuation ownership against Chat, Run and pass identity; retain it across restart and repeated Stop. A normally completed pass consumes its continuation, so the following user message starts the workflow at its entry as before. A Stop racing completed work does not fabricate an unfinished continuation. Preserve canonical history, the Run's authority ceiling and per-Chat concurrency. The v1 graph executes sequentially; a Stop during an Agent-owned tool resumes the owning Agent's model with the recorded tool outcome.

Question suspension (2026-09-21): AnswerQuestion with {questionId, answer} and SkipQuestion with {questionId} join the Chat command surface, both owner-scoped, command-id idempotent, and rejected unless the question belongs to this Chat and is still unanswered. A committed QuestionAskedV1 moves the aggregate to the awaiting_answer phase; QuestionAnsweredV1 or QuestionCancelledV1 returns it to running on the existing resume path, and pause, cancel and terminal states are reachable from awaiting_answer exactly as from awaiting_approval. Recovery restores awaiting_answer from the committed question, and an unanswered question is never answered implicitly by an ordinary message, a retry or a restart. ChatAggregateV1 gains the pending question reference alongside its wait and approval references.

Stopped questions (2026-09-25): Stop closes unanswered questions in the same canonical batch as the stopped reply. Both projection and command validation treat a later stopped/failed/cancelled turn as closing an earlier question, including legacy histories without an explicit question cancellation. A stale answer cannot revive stopped spans. Recovery may redeliver the same committed answer only while its original question's reply remains resumable.
